aqa-definition-nonvariational: Section 1, p.2: the paper describes the AQA term it uses, as a non-variational protocol that simulates a quantum anneal
fs-metric-differs-from-qng: Section 1, p.2: the authors state how their own use of the metric differs from natural gradients
aqa-schedule-definition: Section 2.1, Eqs. 7-9, p.4: the paper defines its own AQA schedule, with gamma+beta=tau and no trivial iteration
aqa-first-order-trotter: Section 2.1, p.4: the authors state their own first order Trotterisation; the similar-results remark is a hedged expectation, not a claimed result
aqa-tau-schedule: Section 2.1, p.5 and Section 7.1, p.17: tau(p)=pi/(2 p^0.25) is the stated schedule
fs-metric-diagonal-formula: Section 2.2, Eqs. 10-14, p.5: Eq. 14 follows by a short derivation shown in the text (Eqs. 11-13) for the state of Eq. 11
fs-eigenstate-zero-metric: Section 2.2, p.6: stated with its condition (eigenstate of X on that qubit) and checkable from Eq. 13 in one line; the argument is brief but it is in the paper
suppressed-mixer-definition: Section 3, Eqs. 18-19, p.7-8: the paper defines its own protocol
thresholded-mixer-definition: Section 3, Eq. 20, p.8: the paper defines its own protocol and fixes Theta = 0.2 for all runs
mixer-naming-unmodified: Section 3, p.8: the paper names the term
problem-qubos-used: Section 4, p.8: the test problems are stated
engineered-qubos-limitation: Section 4, p.9: the authors state that their engineered problems lack the structure of hard problems
weighted-maxcut-construction: Section 4, p.9: the construction of the specialised problem is stated
atif-2022-algorithm1-structure: Section 4, Algorithm 1 and its text, p.9-11: the paper defines its problem generator
mixer-phase-definition: Section 5, Eq. 21, p.12: the paper defines the phase it analyzes, with the branch cut
ionq-3qubit-setup: Section 6 p.14 and Section 8.2 p.24: QUBO, device, date, runs and error bars are stated
ionq-110-upper-bound-method: Section 6, p.14: the measurement method is stated
ionq-suppression-test-setup: Section 6, p.15: the hardware test setting zeta2 = 1/2 is stated
ionq-limitation-no-intuition-total: Section 6, p.17: the authors state they found no clear intuition and chose not to investigate
sec73-specialised-qubo-setup: Section 7.3, p.19: instance parameters are stated; the 'rough features' remark is the authors' motivation
sec73-qaoa-run-setup: Section 7.3, Figure 10 caption, p.21, and Appendix I: runs and iterations are stated
sec73-cdf-setup: Section 7.3, Figure 12 caption, p.22: instance set and p values are stated
sec74-random-qubo-setup: Section 7.4, p.22: the test problem is stated
methods-numerical-setup: Section 8.1, p.24: optimizer, tolerance, iterations and samples are stated
atif-2022-conclusion-future-work: Section 9, p.26: the authors state the work covers only diagonal-element methods and name further options
sec-simulation-ideal-setting: Section 6, p.14: the authors state the simulations assume the ideal setting
case-study-network-setup: Section IV.A, p.4: the scenario nodes are stated
arc-cost-is-delta-v-unit-time: Section IV.A, p.4: arc cost and time of flight are stated
node-roles-and-supply-demand: Table 1, p.5: roles and supply and demand entries are stated; the text layer flattens the table but the quoted rows match
mcnf-formulation-definition: Section III.A, p.2: the paper defines its formulation
dirac3-polynomial-objective-form: Section III.B, Eq. 5, p.3: the objective form the formulation targets is given with its symmetry condition
hamiltonian-penalty-construction: Section IV.B, p.5: the construction is stated
dynamic-range-definition: Section IV.B, p.5: the paper defines the term (the printed example drops the factor 10 in the text layer)
hamiltonian-size: Section IV.B, p.5: the model size and dynamic range of its own instance are stated
dirac3-sampler-parameters-named: Table 3, p.5: the value only names the two parameters; the numbers are lost in the text layer and are not claimed
solution-not-optimal-extra-vehicle: Section IV.B, p.6: the authors state their own solution is not optimal and why
small-coefficients-dynamic-range-limit: Section IV.B, p.6: the authors state the dynamic range limit their own instance approaches (30.78 dB, 25.9 dB without small coefficients)
commodity-flow-table-delivery-note: Section IV.B, p.6: the authors state how the table is to be read
bahengam-2025-conclusion-future-work: Section V, p.7: the authors state the future work they name; it is a statement of intent, not a result
sensor-definition: Section 2, p.2: the paper defines the term for its own use
two-categories: Section 2, p.2: the paper states its own classification
paper-scope-perspective: Section 1, p.2: the authors state their selection is not exhaustive and name the focus
open-entanglement-question: Section 5, p.10: the paper itself states these as open questions; the value claims only that the authors pose them

theory_low.fs-metric-x-basis-measurable: An authors' remark that follows from Eq. 13, not a stated and proved result; 'readily' is their word
theory_low.eigenstate-no-mixing-harmful: The harm claim is argued informally with one example (Eq. 15-17), not proved; the authors' interpretation
theory_low.example-state-minimal-mixing: The text layer gives Fj,j = 2, which cannot be right for Eq. 14 (the value lies in 0 to 1); the item rests on a garbled number in a worked example
theory_low.harmful-relative-phase-mechanism: The harm is argued from Eq. 17 and stated with 'could favor' and 'could globally corrupt'; an authors' interpretation, not a proof
theory_low.mixer-phase-free-variable-intuition: Stated as intuition ('we instead base our intuition'), an authors' interpretation, not a proved result
theory_low.mixer-phase-eight-qubit-analysis: A figure of computed phases for one eight variable QUBO (Figure 4), a measured or simulated result
theory_low.ionq-stated-expectation: The authors' expectation, which they then test; not a settled result
theory_low.edm-implies-t-violation: A standard field argument given in one sentence in a review; not proved in the paper
